messages.subject: predictSE.zip and large abundance predictions
parts:
I've used the function predictSE.zip to generate predictions of brood abundance at a wetland basin level using ZIP hierarchical models (pcount).  The generated predictions make sense at the wetland basin level, but when I scale them up, say to a level of abundance per square mile given a certain set of wetlands, the predictions seem overly large....could this have anything to do with the Poisson distribution I used?  And is there any way to get the predictions to include predictions of "zero"?  This might scale down the higher level summed abundance values and also would seem more realistic to me as I doubt every wetland is occupied....

Any suggestions are appreciated
Thanks
KC

messages.author: cf90957368b0c5d2
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] predictSE.zip and large abundance predictions
parts:
Dear Kaylan,

the predicted abundance returned by predictSE.zip already accounts the
the "0" sites. Have you checked the goodness of fit of your model? If
the model fit is weak, this could explain the discrepancies with your
expectations of the abundance you should have at your sites. It might
also mean that detection probability is low for your sites.

Sincerely,

Marc

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: predictSE.zip and large abundance predictions
parts: Not sure how you are generating your predictions but the lambda from a ZIP model gives you the mean abundance (N) for sites that have the species present.  So if you want a mean abundance across all sites (including the zeros), you need to use N = lambda*(1-psi) where psi is the zero-inflation parameter.  This is pointed out in the help file for pcount.
